rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 488.3, best so far): the oval finish rate reached 0.90 and the s-bend finish rate 0.25, but the slalom still finished 0 of 20 with progress 0.30 and about 1.05 line-loss events per run. Every failure is off_track, and max_error sits at the 0.06 m limit on the s-bend and slalom, so the robot makes brief excursions at sharp direction changes rather than drifting. The trend across iterations is consistent. Cutting mass (0.8 to 0.6 to 0.5 to 0.45 kg) lowered yaw inertia, and each cut raised finish rate and cut max_error. Cutting base_speed from 1.25 to 1.15 also raised s-bend finishes and slalom progress (0.17 to 0.30). Sensor geometry changes in iteration 2 hurt, so the sensors, kp, kd, ki and line_loss stay as they are. Changes: (1) mass 0.45 to 0.40 kg, the minimum allowed, to continue the yaw-inertia trend that has helped every time. (2) base_speed 1.15 to 1.10 to reduce bend-entry speed on the slalom and s-bend. The oval finish time (about 2.4 s at 1.15) should rise to about 2.6 s, which is still under the 3 s limit with some margin. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.35 with some finishes, s-bend finishes above 0.3, and oval finish rate at or above 0.85. Hypotheses: (a) the slalom failure is still driven by yaw inertia and entry speed, so both changes should help; (b) if the oval finish time rises above 2.8 s, speed is becoming the binding constraint and base_speed should not drop further; (c) if slalom line_loss_events stay at 1 or more, the 12 mm sensors are missing the tape on tight bends and a sensor-geometry test is needed. Steering_oscillation (about 0.38 on the oval) is not yet a clear limit, so kd is held at 0.8 for now. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus control_effort to check steering load.
